title: The Open Horizon
premise: Elodie Sterling, captain of the riverboat Kestrel and drowning in debt to the harbormaster Vane, discovers a tide-revealed sea cave holding a drowned smuggler's map to the river's forbidden source, where a legendary glacier vault of pre-war treasure lies sealed. Vane learns of the map and forces Elodie into a brutal partnership, while a rival salvage crew led by the charismatic Cass Merrow races them upstream. As the glacier's calving season approaches, Elodie must choose between paying her debt with blood money or burning the map to protect the river communities who finally claim her as one of their own. In the end, Elodie wrecks the Kestrel deliberately to block Vane's gunboats at the gorge, loses her boat and her debt, and gains something she never had: a place to belong, as the vault floods forever beneath the calving ice.
about_author: Mara Blackwood spent a decade working seasonal river runs in the Pacific Northwest before turning to fiction, and her prose carries the salt-and-diesel grit of that life. She writes adventure stories about people the maps forget.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector's Tide
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Vane gives her thirty days to pay an impossible debt or forfeit the Kestrel. Running a desperate cargo run at night, she watches an unusually low tide expose a sea cave on a charted-as-empty coastline. Emotional beat: suffocating pressure and the first crack of possibility.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Inside the cave she finds a smuggler's skeleton, a brass compass, and a wax-sealed map tracing the river upstream to the glacier source. She pockets it, telling herself it's just salvage. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as practicality.

chapters.title: Vane's Long Fingers
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Elodie and Vane. Vane's clerk spots Elodie asking questions about the upper river; Vane confronts her aboard the Kestrel and reveals he knows the map exists, offering partnership instead of ruin. Emotional beat: the trap closing, invisible no longer.

chapters.title: The Kestrel Goes Upstream
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, with crew members Tam and old engineer Brannick. The Kestrel pushes past the last charted mile into rapids no captain has run. Cass Merrow's salvage boat shadows them from behind. Emotional beat: exhilaration laced with dread.

chapters.title: Riverfolk
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. At a stilt village of river people who've hidden from chart-makers for generations, Elodie is tested, then welcomed, and learns the 'treasure' is their ancestors' sealed refuge. Emotional beat: the first taste of belonging she's never had.

chapters.title: Cass Merrow's Offer
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Merrow intercepts Elodie at a confluence, offering to buy out Vane's claim and split the vault, revealing Vane plans to sell the route to a mining syndicate. Emotional beat: a seductive alternative that asks Elodie to betray the riverfolk anyway.

chapters.title: The Gorge
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Vane's gunboat catches them at a narrow gorge; a running fight costs Brannick his life and forces the Kestrel through a chute that should be impossible. Emotional beat: grief and fury fused into resolve.

chapters.title: Calving Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They reach the glacier face as the ice begins to groan and split; the vault mouth opens with the first calving, a window of hours. Vane arrives with armed men; Cass double-crosses everyone. Emotional beat: terror and awe as the mountain starts to die.

chapters.title: The Weight of Gold
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Inside the vault, Elodie sees the treasure and understands its price: taking it means Vane's syndicate owns the river forever. She triggers the scuttling charges on the Kestrel, sinking her in the gorge to trap Vane's gunboats as the calving begins. Emotional beat: sacrifice as liberation.

chapters.title: The Open Horizon
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Vane drowns with his ambition; Cass escapes empty-handed; the vault seals beneath the ice as the glacier calves. The riverfolk take Elodie in, debt-free, captain of nothing and keeper of everything. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging on an open horizon.
